kinds.title: A Budget that misses the rules

line.text: On today’s estimate a rule is missed, and the speech says so. The OBR’s own forecast will test it again today. The programme may be intact, but its footing is not.
line.short: On today’s estimate a rule is missed. The programme may be intact; its footing is not.

kinds.title: A Budget that met the rules and lost the room

line.text: The arithmetic holds and the party does not. Broken promises, missing priorities or benefit cuts give several groups a reason to vote against it. The rules were never the only audience.
line.short: The arithmetic holds and the party does not: the rules were never the only audience.

kinds.title: A promise broken for a bigger buffer
kinds.fact: Without the change to {breakers}, you would still meet both rules, with {withoutBreak} of headroom.

line.text: The rules did not need the broken promise. It bought a bigger margin, not the programme: a choice you can defend, but a choice. The people it was made to will see the promise, not the margin.
line.short: The rules did not need the broken promise. It bought a bigger margin, not the programme.

line.text: The sums add up by giving less to {cutFrom}, not by taxing more. That comes on top of the squeeze already in the plans for most of what government does.
line.short: The sums add up by giving less to {cutFrom}, not by taxing more.

kinds.title: A cautious Budget: the margin kept, the priorities not

line.text: The margin is kept and the costings are certified, but nothing the Prime Minister asked for is funded. Stability is a kind of success, and the quietest. The backbenches will ask what the margin is for.
line.short: The margin is kept and the costings are certified, but nothing the Prime Minister asked for is funded.

kinds.title: A priority left out with money to spare
kinds.fact: Delivering {leftOut} in full with “{leftOutOption}” would still meet both rules, with {withRoom} of headroom.

line.text: You named {leftOut} a priority in Downing Street and left it unfunded, though the rules would have held with it paid for. The Prime Minister will want to know why.
line.short: You named {leftOut} a priority and left it unfunded, though the rules would have held.

kinds.title: A Budget for {priority} that kept every promise and little headroom

line.text: Every promise kept, every priority funded, and a margin the OBR’s typical forecast error would erase. This is the Budget the programme asked for, on the thinnest ice the rules allow. Whether it holds is up to the next forecast, not you.
line.short: Every promise kept, every priority funded, and a margin the OBR’s typical forecast error would erase.

kinds.title: A Budget for {priority} that delivered what it promised and paid for it

line.text: The priorities are funded, the promises stand and the margin survives. Somebody paid for that, and the who-pays table says who. It is the rarest kind of Budget because it is the hardest: it asks for the money before it spends it.
line.short: The priorities are funded, the promises stand and the margin survives. The who-pays table says who paid.

kinds.title: A Budget that broke a promise to keep another

line.text: The programme is funded and a written commitment was the price. The words are on the record, and so are yours. The people the priorities were for will remember one; the people the promise was made to will remember the other.
line.short: The programme is funded and a written commitment was the price.

line.text: Some of what was agreed in Downing Street is funded and some is not, and the Budget says which. That is most Budgets: a programme trimmed to the money, with the trimming visible. The question the morning papers ask is whether the missing half comes next year.
line.short: Some of what was agreed is funded and some is not, and the Budget says which.

kinds.title: A Budget that moves real money

line.text: Large sums move in both directions, and the rules hold on today’s estimate. Whether they moved the right way is the argument this Budget starts.
line.short: Large sums move, and the rules hold on today’s estimate. The argument starts here.

line.text: Little changed: the plans are much as the Budget found them, with a few adjustments at the edges. Stability of a kind; the argument moves to next year.
line.short: Little changed: the plans are much as the Budget found them.

line.text: The Budget is delivered. The figures above say what it did.
